Want an eye-catching surface design without spending hours nitpicking? Try this: I start with about 0.75lb of clay and throw a 3.5” x 3.5” cylinder with a slight barrel shape. While it’s still on the wheel, I pre-trim a shallow foot, so I don’t have to mess with the texture later. Then comes the magic. Slip applied in an upward and downward spiral motion while the wheel spins. It creates this unpredictable, organic pattern that’s completely unique to each throw. Pro tip: run your slip through a sieve a few times for a buttery smooth consistency. No chunks, no drag, just clean movement. Give it a shot and let me know how it works for you. Ancient Clay Teapot That Changes Color – Traditional Chinese Craftsmanship Discover the fascinating art of traditional Chinese purple clay pottery, where skilled artisans transform natural clay into elegant handmade teapots using centuries-old ceramic techniques. 🍵✨ In this video, craftsmen carefully prepare, filter, shape, and fire special purple clay to create a teapot that is both beautiful and functional. Known in Chinese culture for its ability to “breathe” and enhance the flavor of tea over time, this ancient pottery craft represents one of the finest forms of traditional ceramic artistry and intangible cultural heritage. Every step of the process requires patience, precision, and years of experience. From refining the clay by hand to shaping the teapot with delicate craftsmanship, this traditional art form reflects the beauty of slow living, handmade culture, and historical artisan skills preserved through generations. Long before industrial production existed, handmade clay teapots were treasured for tea ceremonies, daily rituals, and luxury craftsmanship. Their natural texture, elegant shape, and unique firing process make each piece completely one of a kind.
